items.followUp: State two differences between Bohr’s atomic theory and the modern quantum mechanical model of the atom.

rubric.why: This distinguishes Rutherford’s unrestricted electron motion from Bohr’s specific permitted orbits or energy levels.
rubric.description: Rutherford’s model allowed electrons to revolve at any distance; Bohr’s model assigned them fixed orbits or energy levels.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving this contrast between the electron motion in the two models.

rubric.why: Bohr’s explanation of stable, non-radiating orbits addressed the atomic stability that Rutherford’s model could not explain.
rubric.description: Rutherford’s model could not explain atomic stability; Bohr proposed stable permitted orbits in which electrons do not radiate energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the stability limitation of Rutherford’s model and Bohr’s explanation.

modelAnswer: Rutherford’s model allowed electrons to revolve around the nucleus at any distance; Bohr proposed fixed orbits or energy levels for electrons.
Rutherford’s model could not explain atomic stability; Bohr said electrons in permitted orbits do not radiate energy and remain stable.

items.followUp: Write the subshell electronic configuration of Mg²⁺ and state the number of electrons in its outermost shell.

rubric.why: Aluminium has 13 electrons, and Al³⁺ has lost three, leaving 10 electrons in this configuration.
rubric.description: The subshell electronic configuration of Al³⁺ is 1s² 2s² 2p⁶.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the complete, correct subshell configuration.

rubric.why: The outermost occupied shell is n = 2, which contains eight electrons.
rubric.description: Al³⁺ has 8 electrons in its outermost shell.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the correct number of electrons in the outermost shell.

modelAnswer: Al has atomic number 13, so Al³⁺ has 13 − 3 = 10 electrons.

items.followUp: What is a polar covalent bond? Give one example.

rubric.why: Equal sharing of the bonding electron pair is the defining feature of a non-polar covalent bond.
rubric.description: A non-polar covalent bond forms when the bonded atoms share the electron pair equally.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the bonding electron pair is shared equally.

rubric.why: H₂ and Cl₂ are examples of non-polar covalent bonds between identical atoms.
rubric.description: A suitable example is H₂ or Cl₂.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving a correct example.

modelAnswer: A non-polar covalent bond is formed when the bonded atoms share the electron pair equally.
